chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Follow-ups: Sacramento after-hours hours, Hank Fullalove, the San Diego hotel
summary: Details of the Sacramento hours, a tenor player who wrote Westerns, and the Dunbar Hotel and Yesmar in San Diego.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: At the time you took the band to Sacramento for the after-hours gig, was there much music being played there? You mentioned one other after-hours place, the Club Eureka, but were there many other clubs? 'Cause you said something about, when the clubs closed, that everybody came to where you --
Yeah, yeah, but they were all dime-a-dance places, you know. And, like, my hours were from nine

until. That was until the last soul got out of there, you know. Like, we'd go to work at 9:00, we were idle from 9:00 to 12:00. And then when the other places break up, then that's when we'd have to start work. 12:00 until.
The musician Hank Fullalove that you mentioned, you said he wrote Westerns. Did he use his own name?
No, no, he used a pseudonym.
Do you know what the pseudonym was?

No, I don't. I can't recall. He ended up being a Marine, and he really looked the part 'cause he was huge, you know. Wore the uniform, looked good on him. The uniform complimented him. And then, when he got out of the service, he stayed in Seattle, Washington. I haven't seen him since.
The hotel in San Diego, with the nightclub downstairs. Did you think of the name of that?
No.
You were saying earlier, you thought it might be Dunbar.
No, that was the name of the hotel.
But not the club.
No.
But the club was in --
The club was in the hotel, on the
ground floor, in the back.
And the hotel was Dunbar. Then you said the owner of the club's name was Ramsey and he owned another club or another hotel?
Another hotel, around the corner.
And it was called what?
The Yesmar. That's Ramsey spelled backwards.
Was there any music there?
No.
And you said the Honeydripper came down. You're talking about Joe Liggin?
Joe Liggin.
And you mentioned a drummer named Daniels.
I can't recall his first name.
